identity.gender_note: A male given name; the feminine Krishnaa is a separate name.

core_meaning.primary_meaning: Krishna (Sanskrit कृष्ण, Kṛṣṇa) is a male name meaning “black”, “dark” or “dark blue”. It is the name of Krishna, a major deity in Hinduism, worshipped as the eighth avatar of Vishnu and as the Supreme God in his own right.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Sanskrit kṛṣṇá is an adjective meaning “black, dark, dark-blue”, already used in the Rigveda. It goes back to Proto-Indo-European *kr̥snós, “black”, related to Lithuanian kirsnas and the Slavic word for black (Russian чёрный). Krishna is therefore often shown with dark or blue skin; the waning half of the lunar month is called Krishna Paksha, “the dark fortnight”.

etymology.morphology: Sanskrit adjective kṛṣṇá, “black, dark”, used as a proper name.

origin.origin_explanation: Sanskrit; the name of the deity is used as a given name across India and Nepal and in the diaspora.

religion.religious_status: Name of a principal Hindu deity
religion.religious_explanation: Krishna is worshipped as the eighth avatar of Vishnu and, in several traditions, as the Supreme God. He is the speaker of the Bhagavad Gita and is known by many names, including Govinda, Madhava and Gopala. His birth is celebrated each year as Krishna Janmashtami, in late August or early September.

cultural_context.cultural_meaning: As a name of Vishnu, Krishna is the 57th name in the Vishnu Sahasranama.
cultural_context.impact: His many epithets — Govinda, Gopala, Madhava, Hari, Ghanashyam (“dark like a rain cloud”) — are themselves popular given names.

pronunciation.note: Hindi speakers often say KRISH-an; the Sanskrit ṛ is a syllabic r.

name_variants.variant_notes: Krishan and Kishan are North Indian forms, Kanha a pet form, Kannan the Tamil form, Krushna Odia.

known_linguistic_history: The adjective kṛṣṇá appears in the Rigveda.
The life of Krishna is narrated in the Mahabharata, the Harivamsa and the Bhagavata Purana.
historical_context.historical_person_association: Lord Krishna, eighth avatar of Vishnu.

modern_usage.modern_context: A widely used boy's name among Hindus in India, Nepal and the diaspora.

faq.q: Why is Krishna shown with blue skin?
faq.a: Because his name means dark or dark blue; murtis often depict him with black or blue skin.
A major deity, worshipped as the eighth avatar of Vishnu and as the Supreme God in his own right.

faq.q: What are other names of Krishna?
faq.a: Govinda, Gopala, Madhava, Hari, Achyuta, Damodara and Ghanashyam, among many others.
On Krishna Janmashtami, which falls in late August or early September.
